title: source_id committed-input judgment is implemented four times (TermAl launcher JS, TermAl host Rust, Engram reader Rust, Engram's launcher-copy JS); one contract owner, shared conformance fixtures, and removal of copies that exist only by duplication
outcome: The committed-input (source_id) predicate has one written contract with one owner and one shared conformance fixture matrix that every implementation runs. Each remaining implementation has a stated reason to exist, such as a trust boundary. Implementations that exist only because code was copied are removed or replaced by a call to the owner.
acceptance: M1 provides one TermAl host function that invokes the initiating project's explicitly pinned trusted Engram executable and returns the complete strictly parsed source_id object from engram source. The object contains the root commit and tree, submodules with path and actual HEAD (expected pins derive from the root commit), and changes[] from Git status with blob ids produced by the owner using git hash-object --stdin-paths; ignored files are excluded. Exact JSON field names and meanings are agreed with the Engram owner before implementation.

The host preserves the entire source_id object for whole-object comparison and introduces no local reimplementation of its judgment. M1 carries the stage-1 metadata/bootstrap code into a fresh candidate on current master, but does not switch existing consumers or rewrite historical records.

At M1's landing, one aggregate budget of at most 8 seconds, or the caller's shorter deadline, and a 1 MiB output limit covered owner execution and parsing. Later explicitly approved source-operation budget changes replace that budget and remain in force; completing this parent does not restore the retired 8-second limit. Overflow, timeout, missing or untrusted executable, wrong root, malformed or incoherent JSON and process failure return unavailable, with no silent partial object or fallback.

Tests use exact JSON samples and shared fixtures from the Engram owner to cover the agreed new fields, clean and changed input, root/tree identity, actual submodule HEADs, change blob ids, ignored-file exclusion and unavailable/error cases. M1 adds no watcher, hashes no .git directory, derives no full file/index listing and mutates no source or user/global configuration.

The exact M1 candidate has an independent Codex/Claude review pair with no outstanding Medium-or-higher finding, a passing FULL gate and relevant Windows checks before integration through Opus2. Engram E1 may land and install first; M1 then lands after conformance with the installed E1 executable pinned by its supplied hash. Installed/runtime provenance and any required restart or real-repository follow-up are recorded without claiming consumer cutover.

After M1, TermAl's remaining consumers switch to that function one at a time: the launcher's before/after check and host focused and carried credit compare the whole source_id object; new host records carry source_id instead of content-v1 (stored content-v1 and git-commit records stay readable as stored); and TermAl's local predicate copies (host Rust and launcher JS) are removed with no fallback. Each switch is its own reviewed and gated candidate.

After the consumer switches, TermAl's code that creates content-v1 revisions is deleted (today's production producers: src/content_revision.rs, src/content_revision_collisions.rs, src/engram_source_observation_protocol.rs, src/engram_unadmitted_observation.rs, src/engram_registered_closing_baseline.rs, src/ordinary_commit_input.rs and src/acceptance_evaluation.rs, or wherever that code then lives), and TermAl writes no new content-v1 record. Readers of stored content-v1 records remain, and historical records stay readable as stored. This deletion lands last, as its own reviewed and gated candidate, once no consumer uses content-v1.

No automatic agent-facing TermAl surface (prompt or turn notices, tool output, wake or notification text, transcript messages, compaction material) includes an execution_observe request body or a full source_id. Short summaries and root-path lines are allowed. Checked by the review pair on each candidate that touches observation production or agent notices; where an existing behavioural test already exercises an agent notice, it asserts the notice carries no source_id JSON. No new gate and no text-pin test.
